meta.title: Persian B1 Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1000 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Persian → English (see the Persian, recall the meaning) and English → Persian (see an English meaning, recall the Persian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1000 words for an intermediate learner, aligned to B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main points of clear standard input on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure, etc.' — a learner here is able to deal with most situations likely to arise while travelling, to produce simple connected text on familiar topics, and to describe experiences and events, dreams, hopes and ambitions, and briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. The Persian taught is the standard written language of Iran (Farsi), with the everyday spoken form shown beside a word where Tehran speech says it differently. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Persian, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 177 of the 1000 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — work, money and the economy, education, the news, media and technology, government, law and society, the environment and the weather, health and medicine, travel and transport, the household and its chores, relationships and the stages of life, feelings and character, religion and festivals, abstract nouns for ideas, reasons and plans, the connectors that join sentences, and the verbs of thinking, deciding, arguing and changing — and the other 823 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Persian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb, and its spoken form, added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in the Persian script with a romanisation beneath it, Wiktionary's Iranian one (â for the long a, x for kh, š for sh: ketâb, xâne), since the script writes no short vowels; the Persian Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script itself. The 717 nouns show their plural; the 43 verbs show their present stem, which no rule derives from the infinitive and on which every present tense is built, and behind the All forms fold their present, past, future, subjunctive and imperative by person. Real example sentences come with 733 of the 1000 words, three apiece for 357 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, forms and romanisation: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
